Compare Structural Equation Models by an Information Criterion

Source: R/compare_sem.R
compare_sem.Rd

Ranks a set of structural equation models fitted to the same data by one information criterion of sem_information_criteria (BIC by default) and reports, for each model, its difference from the best, its relative weight within the set, and, for the criteria that approximate a log marginal likelihood, the approximate log Bayes factor of the best model over it. The models may be nested or not. A criterion compares models only through their log likelihoods, so before anything is computed the function checks that the log likelihoods are comparable: the same cases and data values, the same observed variables and groups, the same missing data method and mean structure, and the same exogenous observed variables conditioned on. Requires lavaan (in Suggests).

Usage

compare_sem(
  fits,
  criterion = c("BIC", "SABIC", "HBIC", "IBIC", "SPBIC", "AIC"),
  prior_means = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'dmar_compare_sem'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'dmar_compare_sem'
glance(x, ...)

Arguments

fits

A named list of two or more fitted lavaan models: maximum likelihood fits of continuous variables (estimator ML or its robust variants MLM, MLMV, and MLR, which maximize the same likelihood) fitted to the same data. That is, the same cases, data values, observed variables (in any order), and groups; the same missing data method (missing) and mean structure (meanstructure); and, when fixed.x or conditional.x is TRUE, the same exogenous observed variables. Models fitted to summary statistics (sample.cov) are compared when they share the sample moments and N. Two-level models and models fitted with sampling weights are refused, and the criterion can impose further conditions (see sem_information_criteria).

criterion

The criterion: "BIC" (the default), "SABIC", "HBIC", "IBIC", "SPBIC", or "AIC", in either case.

prior_means

For SPBIC, an optional list of prior mean vectors, one per model in the order of fits (and with its names, if named), each in the order of lavaan::coef() of its model. NULL applies the default rule of sem_information_criteria: free loadings and regression coefficients centered at zero and the other free parameters at their estimates. A saturated model needs an explicit prior mean.

x

A dmar_compare_sem table returned by compare_sem().

...

Unused.

Value

A dmar_tbl (class dmar_compare_sem) with one row per model, sorted by the criterion (ties keep the order of fits), and the columns term (the model's name), value (its criterion), delta, relative_weight, log_evidence_best_over_model, and npar (its number of free parameters). The criterion attribute names the criterion, the comparison attribute records what was checked (N, the number of groups, whether the models were fitted to raw data, the missing settings used, the mean structure, the exogenous observed variables conditioned on, and for IBIC and SPBIC the identification), and the sem_information attribute holds the details of each model's sem_information_criteria result, named by model. tidy() returns every column with the criterion beside it, and glance() one row with the criterion, the number of models, N, the best model, its weight, and the difference of the second best.

Details

Differences, Weights, and Evidence

For the criterion values \(C_k\) of the models, \(\Delta_k = C_k - \min_j C_j\) (column delta), and the relative weight of model k is \(\exp(-\Delta_k/2)/\sum_j \exp(-\Delta_j/2)\). BIC, HBIC, IBIC, and SPBIC each approximate \(-2\) times the log marginal likelihood of a model (Bollen, Ray, Zavisca, & Harden, 2012), so \(\exp(-\Delta_k/2)\) approximates the Bayes factor of model k against the best model, the weights approximate the posterior probabilities of the models when every model in the set has the same prior probability (Burnham & Anderson, 2004), and \(\Delta_k/2\) (column log_evidence_best_over_model) approximates the log Bayes factor of the best model over model k. For AIC the weights are Akaike weights, the weight of evidence that each model is the one of the set closest to the data generating process in Kullback-Leibler discrepancy (Burnham & Anderson, 2004); they are not posterior probabilities under equal prior odds, and the log evidence column is NA. SABIC rests on the minimum description length principle rather than on a marginal likelihood, so its weights carry no further interpretation and its log evidence column is NA too. So it is for every criterion of models fitted by two-stage maximum likelihood (missing = "two.stage" or "robust.two.stage"), whose criteria are those of Lai (2021): built from the complete data normal log likelihood at the EM estimates of the means and covariances, they select in large samples the model complete data would select, but they are not a likelihood of the observed data and approximate no marginal likelihood (see sem_information_criteria).

Every weight is conditional on the set of models compared: adding or removing a model changes all of them, and none of them says how well a model fits in absolute terms (sem_fit_measures speaks to that). Nor do the weights carry the sampling variability of the criteria; the uncertainty of the selection itself is not estimated.

What Is Checked

Each model must have converged to an admissible solution and have a log likelihood the criteria are defined on (see sem_information_criteria for what is refused and why). Then every model is compared with the first, and the first difference found is reported with the two models it concerns and what to do.

Data

The same groups, the same observed variables, the same number of cases, the same cases, and the same data values (or, for models fitted to summary statistics, the same sample moments). The order of the variables does not matter; a set of different variables does, since a log likelihood is a density of the variables it models.

Missing data

The same missing data method. Listwise deletion, FIML, and the two-stage method give different likelihoods, and two listwise fits of different variables keep different cases. The two two-stage settings, missing = "two.stage" and "robust.two.stage", count as one method: they fit the same EM moments by the same likelihood and differ only in their standard errors and test statistic, which no criterion uses. Two-stage fits must also share the auxiliary variables of their first stage (lavaan's aux), since those change the EM estimates their log likelihoods are evaluated at. A two-stage fit whose first stage read cases observed on an auxiliary variable but on none of the model's variables, which lavaan leaves out of its N, is compared by the criterion sem_information_criteria computes for it with every case the first stage read, its log likelihood and the N of the penalty included (in several groups held together by a constraint, at the estimates with every case read, which move with the groups' counts), and a line under the table says so; such a fit and the fit fa_confirmatory(missing = "two_stage") or measurement_invariance returns for the same data count the same cases.

Mean structure

The same meanstructure setting: without a mean structure lavaan leaves the saturated means out of the parameter count, which moves every criterion by an amount that depends on the setting.

Exogenous variables

With fixed.x = TRUE (the default of lavaan::sem()) or conditional.x = TRUE, lavaan's log likelihood is the density conditional on the exogenous observed variables, the joint density less the marginal density of those variables, and its parameter count leaves out their moments. Two models that treat different variables as exogenous therefore have log likelihoods of different conditional distributions, whose difference can be hundreds of points for two saturated models of the same three variables. Models with the same exogenous variables are compared, and the others are refused with the advice to refit every model with fixed.x = FALSE.

Identification

For IBIC, and for SPBIC under its default prior, every latent variable of every model must be identified the same way (each by a marker indicator, or each by a fixed variance), since both criteria change with the identification even though the likelihood does not (see sem_information_criteria). A set that uses both is refused, also when each model mixes them in the same way: one identification throughout is a convention that can be stated and reported, and it catches the models that differ, which may share no latent variable to compare. Within one data set the units of the observed variables are shared, but an IBIC ranking still depends on them.

References

Bollen, K. A., Harden, J. J., Ray, S., & Zavisca, J. (2014). BIC and alternative Bayesian information criteria in the selection of structural equation models. Structural Equation Modeling, 21(1), 1–19. doi:10.1080/10705511.2014.856691

Bollen, K. A., Ray, S., Zavisca, J., & Harden, J. J. (2012). A comparison of Bayes factor approximation methods including two new methods. Sociological Methods & Research, 41(2), 294–324. doi:10.1177/0049124112452393

Burnham, K. P., & Anderson, D. R. (2004). Multimodel inference: Understanding AIC and BIC in model selection. Sociological Methods & Research, 33(2), 261–304. doi:10.1177/0049124104268644

Lai, K. (2021). Using information criteria under missing data: Full information maximum likelihood versus two-stage estimation. Structural Equation Modeling, 28(2), 278–291. doi:10.1080/10705511.2020.1780925

See also

sem_information_criteria for the criteria of one model and what each assumes, sem_fit_measures for the fit of each model in absolute terms, and the vignette vignette("sem_fit_measures", package = "DMAR").

Examples

# One factor against two correlated factors for six of the
# holzinger_swineford tests.
one <- lavaan::cfa(
  "g =~ t1_visual_perception + t2_cubes + t4_lozenges +
        t6_paragraph_comprehension + t7_sentence + t9_word_meaning",
  data = holzinger_swineford)
two <- lavaan::cfa(
  "visual  =~ t1_visual_perception + t2_cubes + t4_lozenges
   textual =~ t6_paragraph_comprehension + t7_sentence + t9_word_meaning",
  data = holzinger_swineford)
x <- compare_sem(list(one_factor = one, two_factors = two))
x
#>  term        value     delta  relative_weight log_evidence_best_over_model npar
#>  two_factors 10947.060 0.000  1.000           0.000                        13  
#>  one_factor  11020.221 73.161 0.000           36.581                       12  
#> 
#> Criterion: BIC (smaller is preferred); N = 301; 2 models.
#> Checked: the same cases and data values, observed variables, missing data method (missing = "listwise"), and mean structure (meanstructure = FALSE); no exogenous variables conditioned on.
#> relative_weight: approximate posterior probability of each model within this set under equal prior odds; log_evidence_best_over_model: approximate log Bayes factor of the best model over each.
generics::glance(x)
#>   criterion n_models   N  best_model best_weight delta_second
#> 1       BIC        2 301 two_factors           1     73.16114

# The same comparison by SPBIC, under its default prior.
compare_sem(list(one_factor = one, two_factors = two), criterion = "SPBIC")
#>  term        value     delta  relative_weight log_evidence_best_over_model npar
#>  two_factors 10939.120 0.000  1.000           0.000                        13  
#>  one_factor  11008.596 69.475 0.000           34.738                       12  
#> 
#> Criterion: SPBIC (smaller is preferred); N = 301; 2 models.
#> Checked: the same cases and data values, observed variables, missing data method (missing = "listwise"), and mean structure (meanstructure = FALSE); no exogenous variables conditioned on; identification: marker indicator.
#> relative_weight: approximate posterior probability of each model within this set under equal prior odds; log_evidence_best_over_model: approximate log Bayes factor of the best model over each.
